verdict.rationale: NVIDIA's RTX 5080 page pitches the card for development, with GPU-optimized SDKs and PyTorch backends. The CUDA Toolkit page documents a GPU-accelerated development environment, and community compute benchmarks show the 5080 running compute workloads. However, no evidence shows CUDA documentation explicitly listing the RTX 5080 (or its Blackwell compute capability) as a supported target. Missing for 10: an explicit CUDA supported-GPU or compute-capability listing that names the RTX 5080, minimum CUDA/driver version requirements for this part, and hands-on reports of building and shipping CUDA kernels on it.

support.subject: As a developer, I can ship GPU-compute workloads on the vendor's toolchain — CUDA or ROCm/HIP documentation lists this part as a supported target

citations.quote: Access curated, GPU-optimized SDKs and models, and maximize performance across Windows ML, Ollama, PyTorch, and other inference backends.
accelerate your gaming, creating, productivity, and development
The NVIDIA® CUDA® Toolkit provides a development environment for creating high-performance, GPU-accelerated applications.
In compute benchmarks, the 4080 Super is clearly behind the 5080 and 5090 in many cases.
